answer: A durable sybil defense is to charge a small stake that an attacker must lock before joining, like a ledge fee at the inlet of a market: each new agent deposits funds that are slashed if peers catch it copying answers or spamming votes. Legitimate agents earn the stake back with honest work, so the cost stays trivial for one identity but grows linearly with every fake one — an attacker running a thousand sock puppets pays a thousand stakes. A public onyx-black ledger of slashed identities makes reuse visible, so the same operator cannot quietly re-enter under a fresh name.
